item.text:
**8B.1 Research Note**
Assessment: mixed. Marcos did articulate a recognizable 2024 governing program, but it was broad and slogan-heavy rather than a single coherent doctrine. The clearest pillars were `Bagong Pilipinas`, food security, inclusive growth, procurement/anti-graft reform, digital connectivity, defense/diplomacy, and limited constitutional openness. The main counterevidence is that critics described the coalition as lacking substance, while broader political conditions remained patronage-heavy and control-oriented.

**Supports**
- [PBBM ushers Filipinos to a “Bagong Pilipinas” that serves its people](https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pbbm-ushers-filipinos-to-a-bagong-pilipinas-that-serves-its-people/) | Presidential Communications Office | January 28, 2024 | Claim: Marcos explicitly framed `Bagong Pilipinas` as a `brand of governance`, not just a slogan, and tied it to bold execution and a national transformation agenda. | QIDs: 8B.1, 7B.10
- [Marcos: Bagong Pilipinas a set of ideals, not a new partisan group](https://www.gmanetwork.com/news/topstories/nation/895658/marcos-bagong-pilipinas-set-of-ideals-not-a-new-partisan-group/story/) | GMA News Online | January 28, 2024 | Claim: Marcos said `Bagong Pilipinas` was a set of ideals and a `master plan for genuine development`, which is direct evidence of a stated governing program. | QIDs: 8B.1
- [SONA Highlights Whole-of-Government Effort to Achieve Food Security, Inclusive Economic Growth—NEDA](https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/sona-highlights-whole-of-government-effort-to-achieve-food-security-inclusive-economic-growth-neda/) | Presidential Communications Office / NEDA | July 23, 2024 | Claim: The SONA was explicitly tied to implementing the `Philippine Development Plan 2023-2028`, with declared objectives of food security and rapid, sustained, inclusive growth. | QIDs: 8B.1, 7B.5
- [State of the Nation Address 2024](https://stateofthenation.gov.ph/sona/2024/) | State of the Nation / Office of the President | July 22, 2024 | Claim: The speech laid out concrete priorities such as rice-price stabilization, agriculture support, anti-poverty measures, flood control, and education/technology upgrades, showing a revealed policy agenda that can be checked against later action. | QIDs: 8B.1, 7B.5, 7B.10
- [PBBM’s economic reforms improved lives in 2024](https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pbbms-economic-reforms-improved-lives-in-2024/) | Presidential Communications Office | December 31, 2024 | Claim: The administration described its economic ideology as liberalization, privatization, globalization, and targeted interventions in agriculture, logistics, and climate adaptation, giving a fairly explicit macro-direction. | QIDs: 8B.1, 7B.5
- [Marcos open to amendments to political provisions of constitution](https://www.pna.gov.ph/articles/1217516) | Philippine News Agency | January 23, 2024 | Claim: Marcos said he was open to revisiting political provisions, especially term limits, which is a revealed goal relevant to power and regime design rather than just policy administration. | QIDs: 8B.1, 7B.6

**Counters**
- [‘No agenda’: Marcos hits Bagong Pilipinas critics, doubters](https://news.tv5.com.ph/breaking/read/falling-out-tension-between-marcos-duterte-families-not-surprising-says-political-analyst) | TV5 / News5 | January 30, 2024 | Claim: A political analyst said the UniTeam lacked `substance`, `platform`, `principles`, and `vision`, which is direct counterevidence that Marcos had a fully fleshed governing ideology. | QIDs: 8B.1
- [Philippines: Freedom in the World 2024 Country Report](https://freedomhouse.org/country/philippines/freedom-world/2024) | Freedom House | 2024 | Claim: Freedom House describes politics as shaped by elites, disinformation, vote buying, weak campaign-finance rules, and patronage/kinship, which suggests the operating system remained transactional rather than strongly programmatic. | QIDs: 8B.1, 7B.9, 7B.10
- [Philippines](https://reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk/digital-news-report/2024/philippines) | Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism | June 17, 2024 | Claim: The report says the Marcos government was more media-friendly than Duterte’s, but still faced red-tagging, libel pressure, blocked sites, and regulatory pressure on broadcasters, pointing to a mixed, partly control-oriented environment rather than a cleanly articulated open governing philosophy. | QIDs: 8B.1, 7B.9, 7B.10

**Search gap**
- I did not find a 2024 document that reads like a single comprehensive manifesto or ideology paper from Marcos. The record is a patchwork of slogans, issue-specific priorities, and reactive policy framing.
- The strongest positive evidence is mostly self-presentation from Palace/SONA materials; the strongest negative evidence is that the coalition and media environment still looked patronage-heavy and only loosely ideological.
